SUMMARY: hairstyle a long side ponytail with softly swept bangs; costume a sleek armored bodysuit — thin, long plates on the shoulders, arms and legs that follow her curves closely; design idea nested off-centre circular layers fastened at a single golden central hub, expressing the heliocentric revolution; face distinct listed features; expression quiet and thoughtful

A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Copernicium (코페르니슘) itself — the sovereign of the Copernicium Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: early thirties — a poised, graceful face with soft contours; at most faint lines, no deep folds or under-eye bags.
Face — her own: an elegant, refined presence; fair skin; oval face; almond-shaped eyes of natural size; amber eyes; straight brows of natural fullness; a nose with a soft, rounded tip, of natural size; medium-full lips of natural width.
Body and hair: slender-limbed yet full-busted with rounded hips and a narrow waist build; a long side ponytail with softly swept bangs; pale liquid-silver hair with a bright sun-gold crown, circled by thin rings of light like orbits.
Expression: a quiet, thoughtful look, lips lightly closed.
Her element, carried in her design: copernicium: a synthetic superheavy element first made in 1996, a single atom caught by firing zinc ions at a lead target, and named on the birthday of the astronomer who put the sun, not the Earth, at the centre of the heavens, a quiet revolution he held back for decades and printed only in the year he died; its first proposed symbol had to be changed because it had once belonged to another element; it sits below zinc, cadmium and mercury, its outer electrons held so tightly that it was predicted to flow like mercury or drift like a noble gas, and a few atoms showed it to be a volatile metal that clings only lightly to gold.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — MECHA
Costume: she is a female mecha personification — plates, joints, binders and glow lines carry the traits above; the plates must read as solid armor with visible joints, not as cloth or a gown; a back unit may carry the motif. A long coat of rigid liquid-silver plates from the shoulders to below the knees, open at the front over deep celestial-blue body armor, an angular high collar, fine pale elliptical orbit lines engraved across the coat plates, a small golden sun-disc core at the chest with tiny silver beads set in orbit around it; the plates must read as solid armor, not a gown.
Silhouette: a sleek armored bodysuit — thin, long plates on the shoulders, arms and legs that follow her curves closely. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette.
Design idea: nested off-centre circular layers fastened at a single golden central hub, expressing the heliocentric revolution.
Colours: liquid mercury silver, sun-centre gold, deep celestial blue, pale orbit-line white.
Exposure (bold): her mecha frame is cut open by design in only these places — bare shoulders and upper arms between pauldron and gauntlet, and a deep open chest window with natural cleavage framed by the chest plates; everywhere else she stays fully plated. The plates stay on, fitted and symmetrical, with skin clearly showing in each opening. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; keep the plate material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: year 2200, a city of rings circling an artificial sun: a small sun hangs at the centre while ring habitats great and small turn slowly around it, each in its own orbit, gardens of golden collector panels that always turn to face it, and silver shuttle stations passing between the rings.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: the scene's own light, rendered the way this style renders light and skin.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Cn) and atomic number (112) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish.
